research_question: In people of any age requiring a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC), what is the effect of non-valved PICCs compared with PICCs with integrated valve technology (proximal or distal valves) on catheter occlusion during catheter dwell time?
control_label: Valved PICC (integrated proximal or distal valve; multiple valved arms combined)
outcome_description: Catheter occlusion during catheter dwell time: number of participants (or catheters) with partial or complete occlusion, including withdrawal occlusion, lumen blockage, occlusion requiring thrombolytic/declotting therapy, or occlusion leading to catheter removal. Analysed as a dichotomous outcome (events/total per arm). Catheter failure, venous thromboembolism, infection/CLABSI, breakage, dislodgement and other complications are NOT pooled.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means FEWER catheter occlusions in the non-valved PICC group than in the valved PICC group (i.e. favours non-valved PICCs).
search_queries: valved versus non-valved peripherally inserted central catheter occlusion trial
PICC valve technology Groshong PASV catheter occlusion randomized controlled comparison
open-ended versus valved PICC complications effect quantitative study
inclusion_criteria: Participants of any age (neonatal, paediatric or adult) in any clinical setting who received a peripherally inserted central catheter
Compares non-valved (open-ended) PICCs with valved PICCs (proximal or distal integrated valve), in any design including randomised, quasi-experimental and observational comparative studies
Reports some quantitative data on catheter occlusion (events and denominators, rates, proportions, or an effect estimate such as an odds/risk ratio)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, opinion pieces, commentaries, case reports, protocols or purely theoretical papers)
No comparison between a non-valved PICC group and a valved PICC comparison group (e.g. single-arm studies, or comparisons of catheter material, tip design or taper alone)
No quantitative occlusion data from which an effect size can be computed (no events/totals, proportions, test statistics or odds/risk ratios)
Completely unrelated to PICCs or to catheter occlusion (e.g. only non-PICC devices, or only reporting failure, thrombosis, infection or breakage without occlusion data)
moderators_to_extract: Study design (RCT vs quasi-experimental vs observational)
Valve type in comparator (proximal vs distal vs mixed/combined arms)
Clinical setting and indication (oncology, parenteral nutrition, home infusion, ICU)
Unit of analysis (participants vs catheters) and sample size category
effect_size_note: Dichotomous data: extract occlusion events and totals per arm; combine multiple valved arms into a single comparator group. Unit of analysis = participants where available, otherwise catheters (record which). Random-effects pooling with heterogeneity assessed via I-squared.
